replicated_originals.reference: Thiede, Anderson & Therriault (2003) Accuracy of metacognitive monitoring affects learning of texts

A.reason: The paper states its first goal is to conceptually replicate the delayed-keyword effect on relative accuracy, which K. W. Thiede originally proposed. Its procedure follows Thiede et al. (2003) explicitly: the same instruction that participants might be asked to generate keywords, and the same Titanic keyword example ('identical to Thiede et al. 2003'). The replication hypothesis (delayed keywords vs. no keywords on gamma relative accuracy) was supported.

B.reason: Cited as ref [36], one of several studies showing the keyword effect, as the model for the inference-question posttest, and for its discussion of delayed vs. immediate judgments. The paper's replicated procedure and its framing of the effect's origin point to Thiede et al. (2003), not to this follow-up study of the mechanism.

notes: The paper replicates 'the keyword effect' as a body of work (De Bruin et al. 2011; Thiede et al. 2003; [36]; [38]). Thiede et al. 2003 is taken as the original because it is the pioneering study and the paper copies its procedure. Thiede et al. 2005 (B) is a borderline case: it also contrasts delayed keywords with no keywords, so a reviewer could reasonably count it as a second original.
